messages:
Jamie: Quick heads-up — ran a token-level trace for /v1/stream on the dedicated pool. Seeing repeated ~60–120ms gaps where server appears idle between chunk builds and network send. Posted a short waterfall and pprof to S3: https://s3.redwood/profiles/1793456789.trace

Priya: Can you paste the kernel selection lines? wondering if we're falling back to slower kernels for some seq/bs combos.

Jamie: Sure, pasted a snippet below from the runtime log:
```
[2026-03-12T15:12:45Z] kernel_select: chosen=quant_q4_0_kvopt seq=512 bs=8 est_ms=3.4 fallback_kernel=fp16_attention
[2026-03-12T15:12:46Z] chunk_builder: build_ms=78 kv_lookup_ms=12 assemble_ms=3
[2026-03-12T15:12:46Z] network_send: queued_ms=95 sockets_write_ms=2
```
Notice the chunk_builder build_ms spikes to ~70–90ms intermittently.

Marcus: That build_ms spike smells like KV cache misses + mem-copy overhead. We saw similar when eviction churned in the new allocator. Is the KV hit rate stable?

Jamie: KV hit rate drops from 99.6% to ~92% under bursty traffic in the trace. Hotspots line up with eviction events.

Lin: We don't currently expose a token-level server->client split metric. We should add: token_build_ms, kv_lookup_ms, kernel_compute_ms, network_send_ms, client_render_ms. Then a per-route KPI aggregation (p50/p95/p99).

Priya: Agreed. Also check whether batching heuristics are re-batching at the tail — if batches shrink to bs=1/2, kernel selection moves to fallbacks with higher latency. Can you include batch size histogram for the same trace?

Jamie: Attached histogram in the trace. We do see tails with effective bs dropping to 2 for ~30s.

Marcus: Short-term mitigation: prewarm KV for hot prefixes and bump cache size heuristically for routes with high seq variance. Medium-term: make kernel selection factor in observed batch-size distribution (not just current batch).

Lin: For dashboards — proposal for PromQL strings (rough draft):
```
# server token build times p95 per route
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_build_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
# split server vs network
sum(rate(token_build_sum[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(token_build_count[5m])) by (route)
```
We should also add a derived metric: server_to_client_gap_ms = token_send_ts - token_ready_ts.

profiling-bot: profile uploaded to s3: https://s3.redwood/profiles/1793456789.trace (size 4.3MB) :mag:

Priya: Nice. For immediate triage, can we instrument the runtime to emit a small log event on eviction with the active batch size at that moment? That will prove causality.

Jamie: I can add that and roll a short patch to the canary tomorrow morning. Also will add the token-level split metrics to the debug pipeline.

deploy-bot: Canary build 2026.03.13-0815 queued for eng-runtime-canary.

Marcus: If the canary shows the same pattern, plan B: temporary kernel pinning for the dedicated pool to avoid fallback path for 256–512 seq until we fix batching. :thinking_face:

Lin: I can draft the dashboard panels (per-route p95, server/net split, kv-hit-rate overlay) — will share a mock in #eng-runtime-dashboards later today.

Jamie: Thanks — short checklist I'll follow: 1) add eviction+batch log line, 2) emit token-level split metrics, 3) short canary with kernel pin option, 4) prewarm script for hot prefixes. Will update thread after first canary.

Priya: Thanks @Jamie — ping me when the canary is up and I will run a load profile that reproduces the burst. :thumbsup:
